questions.q: What does an 'account' record represent in a CRM?
options: A specific potential deal
The company (or household) a business sells to
A single unqualified lead
A support ticket
questions.explain: An account represents the organization being sold to — company-level information like industry, size, and billing address.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a lead and a contact, according to this lesson?
options: A lead is always a company, while a contact is always a person
There is no meaningful difference between the two
A contact must always be converted into a lead before it can be used
A lead is a single, unqualified record of interest, while a contact is a real person already linked to an account
questions.explain: A lead exists before anyone has decided it's worth pursuing; a contact is a verified person tied to an account the business is actively engaging.

questions.q: What happens when a lead is 'converted'?
options: The lead record is permanently deleted
The lead automatically becomes a closed-won deal
The CRM splits the one lead record into an account, a contact, and usually an opportunity
The lead is merged into an existing support case
questions.explain: Conversion turns one messy, unqualified lead record into three clean, connected records.

questions.q: What three things does an opportunity typically track?
options: A job title, a phone number, and an email address
A billing address, an industry, and a website
A support ticket number, a priority, and a resolution date
A dollar value, an expected close date, and a stage
questions.explain: An opportunity represents a specific potential deal, tracked by value, expected close date, and how far along it is in the sales process.

questions.q: Why can one account have multiple contacts, according to this lesson?
options: Because Salesforce requires at least three contacts per account
Because a buying decision often involves several real people at the same company, such as an evaluator, a budget approver, and an end user
Because each contact represents a different company
Because leads cannot be linked to more than one account
questions.explain: Keeping each person as a separate contact under one account lets a rep see the whole buying committee, not just one point of contact.
